provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Return up to k candidate indices ranked by descending finite score.

Candidates are unique int64 indices into a floating score vector on the
same device. Empty candidates and zero k yield empty indices. Uses native
torch.topk ordering, including its tie behavior; no stable or cross-device
tie ordering is promised. Selection is discrete, but gathering scores by
the returned indices preserves their ordinary autograd path. No label or
batch-size interpretation is built in; the caller determines candidates/k.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Return -sum(float32(p<threshold)*weights*log(p+offset))/B/K.

Finite B,K float32/float64 probabilities lie in [0,1]; finite weights lie in [0,1]
and match shape, dtype and device. The strict mask has no gradient, while
probability and weight paths retain autograd. Averages over all entries,
including unselected entries. Inputs and control values remain unchanged.
Offset is explicit; p+offset>1 can yield a negative contribution, so callers
must select controls appropriate for their objective. No labels or domains
are inferred. Float32 mask and ordered divisions preserve source arithmetic.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Return 1-prod(1-p)*(1-sigmoid(b)) per row, preserving autograd.

Inputs are nonempty finite B,K floating probability tensors in [0,1] and
a finite one-element floating baseline logit on the same device/dtype.
The baseline is caller-owned; this operation creates no trainable state.
No clamping, detachment, normalization or hidden class/feature ordering.
Probabilistic interpretation requires caller-established assumptions about
the events; this algebra alone does not establish independence or calibration.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Return a tensor view cropped around each selected axis's integer center.

Each window starts at dimension//2-width//2 and contains exactly width
elements. This explicitly determines even/odd alignment. Unselected axes,
dtype, device and autograd are preserved. No padding, copying, reduction,
channel interpretation or normalization. Returned storage aliases the input.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Return float64 coordinate rows multiplied, divided, then shifted per axis.

Computes (rows*numerator)/denominator-offset in that order, without
precomputing a scale ratio. Signed scales are allowed. All vectors must
match the row width; empty row sets are valid. Input is preserved and output
is newly allocated. No axis reordering, absolute value, geometric clipping,
orientation inference, unit assumptions, or annotation-sentinel policy.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Resample a finite 3D array; return array and effective axis spacing.

Shape is rounded from shape*spacing/requested_spacing using NumPy rounding.
Interpolation uses scipy.ndimage.zoom with nearest boundary extension,
default prefiltering and grid_mode=False. Output retains the input dtype;
integer interpolation therefore retains SciPy's integer rounding behavior.
Effective spacing is spacing*input_shape/output_shape and can differ from
requested spacing. Axis order and physical units are caller-defined; no
orientation, intensity normalization, segmentation or coordinate mapping.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Remove margins and reconstruct finite T,Z,Y,X,... tiles as Z,Y,X,... .

Trailing payload axes are optional and opaque. Output is float32, retaining
the padded grid extent rather than trimming to the original volume shape.
Requires every tile in X-fastest order; no overlap averaging or missing-tile
imputation. Side and margin are input-grid units, divided by output stride.
Rejects nonfinite input or float32 overflow; leaves caller arrays unchanged.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Split finite C,Z,Y,X arrays into ordered edge-padded cubic tiles and grid.

Returns T,C,Z,Y,X tiles and a three-integer grid, with X varying fastest.
Each tile has side_len+2*margin samples per spatial axis. Boundary values
are extended by edge padding. Retains input dtype; no intensity transform,
coordinate generation or model inference. Caller supplies spatial units.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Repeat each row by the sum of multiplicities for strictly exceeded thresholds.

Thresholds are finite, strictly increasing caller-unit values, including
negative values when appropriate. Multiplicities are nonnegative integers.
Rows below or equal to the first threshold disappear; there is no implicit
base copy. Retains input row order and dtype, returning a fresh matrix.
Empty row populations are valid. No labels, units or sampling policy inferred.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.

provider_contracts.operation_contract:
Select indices without replacement, recomputing floored softmax each draw.

Each draw divides remaining scores by temperature, normalizes exponentials,
floors probabilities, then normalizes again. The floor applies before the
second normalization, not as a guaranteed final lower bound. If k covers
all candidates, return original order without consuming RNG state. Empty
vectors and k=0 are valid. Uses a local RandomState from a seed, or advances
the supplied RandomState; never uses NumPy's global RNG. No model fitting.
provider_contracts.state_contract: Runtime model, factory, RNG and tensor objects remain in-process unless an explicit bytes export is requested.
